name: diagnostics_no_status_feedback
description: Investigate a complaint that the customer operated a device physically/locally (flipping a switch, a sensor tripping) and NuCore didn't show the new status -- the device -> NuCore direction, not a control complaint. Runs the full mandatory investigation (core services, protocol enabled/connected, PLM link-record sanity check, and optionally a specific device's own link) in one call, in the correct order, and returns a diagnosis plus a recommended fix when it finds one. Prefer this over manually replaying get_full_system_config/get_core_services_status yourself for a status-feedback complaint. Use diagnostics_not_responding instead for a control/communication complaint (customer can't control/reach a device, or nothing happens when they try) -- that's the default reading of a vague complaint that doesn't clearly describe a physical/local action.

protocol.description: The device's real protocol family (e.g. "insteon", "zwave", "zigbee", "matter") -- from get_device_family, never guessed from the device's name. Only "insteon" has real automated diagnosis today; other protocols return a plain not-yet-supported result.

device_id.description: The customer-named device, if they named one. Optional even after system-level checks pass -- for insteon, omitting it samples 1-2 representative devices automatically rather than requiring you to pick one.
